value_stream.name: Philippine Multi-Region LGU & Local Regulatory Compliance

fields.Participants: VP Legal, Store Managers, Regional Managers, Government Relations
fields.Trigger: New LGU administration or periodic engagement

Automation Opportunity: - Official-contact directory with election-cycle expiry reminders; engagement-log auto-populated from calendar/visit records; gift-register workflow for ABC-officer review
Controls: - CTL-459 (ensure controlled execution — LGU Relationship & Regulatory Analytics (PA-76.3).)
- CTL-459 (ABC / anti-bribery — links to VS-86.3 / W159): all LGU engagement within the gift/sponsorship policy; operational: VS-132 conduct review during election periods
Pain Points / Risks: - **ABC exposure risk**: relationship-building can shade into gift-giving or sponsorship that violates the anti-bribery policy (links to VS-86.3 / W159); mitigated by the VS-132 conduct framework, a documented gift register, and the ABC-officer review of any LGU sponsorship

- **Post-election-void risk**: an election loss displaces the officials BuildRight had relationships with, leaving a cold start with the new administration; mitigated by the 3-year post-election cycle in step 3 and relationship-building at the staff (not just elected) level who persist across administrations
System Touchpoints: - Stakeholder CRM (links to VS-104 government affairs, VS-13 / W209 community relationship) — the official-contact directory and engagement log per LGU
- VS-132 (corporate political engagement & election compliance) — the conduct framework for engagement during election periods (no contribution violations)
- Communication/distribution (links to VS-07 / W571) — engagement coordination across the regional/store layer
Time Estimate: ~6 hours/week VP Legal strategy + Store/Regional Manager day-to-day absorbed into W2673 + ~40 hours per 3-year post-election cycle (distributed) = **~325 hours/year** VP Legal (itemized), plus absorbed Government Relations partner-management time, plus field-team time absorbed.

steps.activity: VP Legal maintains the LGU relationship strategy: key officials per location (mayor, councilors, BPLO head, fire marshal, barangay captains — the same contacts the W2673 barangay work engages at the lowest tier); tracks the 3-year local-election cycle that resets the official set; plans the engagement calendar

Store Managers maintain the day-to-day relationships at barangay level (W2673); Regional Managers handle city/municipal level; Government Relations handles province and the ARTA (Anti-Red Tape Authority, RA 11032) interface for systemic friction

VP Legal conducts the post-election engagement cycle (every 3 years, synchronized with the local-election cycle): meets newly-seated officials, introduces BuildRight's footprint and economic contribution, renews the relationship baseline; obtains the updated official contact directory

fields.Participants: Finance Analyst, Tax Manager, Finance Controller
fields.Trigger: Annual benchmarking cycle — Multi-LGU Regulatory Cost Benchmarking

Automation Opportunity: - Cost-per-store auto-aggregated from the P&L and tax masters; heat-map auto-refreshed annually with year-over-year delta highlighting
Controls: - CTL-459 (ensure controlled execution — LGU Relationship & Regulatory Analytics (PA-76.3).)
- CTL-459 (tax-cost accuracy — links to VS-79 / W349 corporate tax & statutory reporting audit); operational: Finance Controller sign-off on the benchmark before it feeds site-selection
Pain Points / Risks: - **Hidden-cost-blindness risk**: the benchmark captures cash cost (taxes, fees) but misses the soft cost of a slow-permit LGU (staff time, opening delays); mitigated by including compliance-staff time and penalty incidence in the cost composite

- **Stale-benchmark risk**: an LGU's cost ranking from a year ago no longer reflects a recent ordinance change (links to W2680); mitigated by the benchmark refresh tying to the W2680 change-monitoring output
System Touchpoints: - Store-P&L (links to VS-17 / W26 budget) — the revenue and local-tax lines feeding the % computation
- Tax master (links to VS-29 / W293, VS-79) — LGU rates and fee schedules
- Analytics/BI (links to VS-27 / W113) — the cost heat map and benchmark visualization
Time Estimate: ~2 weeks Analyst compilation + ~1 week benchmark + presentation absorbed = **~120–150 hours/year** Finance Analyst + Tax Manager.

steps.activity: Finance Analyst compiles the total regulatory cost per store: local business tax (W2678), real property tax (W2679), permit fees (W2670 suite), penalties incurred, compliance-staff time allocation; expresses each as % of the store's revenue (a like-for-like comparison metric across high- and low-revenue stores)

Analyst benchmarks across the ~150 LGUs (per W54): most-expensive (Metro Manila, Cebu City), most-business-friendly (the LGUs offering tax holidays per W2689), penalty incidence; produces a cost heat map across the Philippine footprint

Finance Controller presents to COO and VP Strategy: the cost heat map influences new-store site selection (links to VS-20 / W116 site selection) and identifies LGUs where BuildRight should negotiate incentives (links to W2689)

fields.Participants: Internal Auditor, Legal Compliance Officer, VP Legal

workflows.name: LGU Regulatory Compliance Audit & Gap Analysis

Automation Opportunity: - Risk-based sample selection auto-derived from the W2677 dashboard (flag locations for audit); finding-recurrence auto-detected across audit cycles
Controls: - CTL-459 (ensure controlled execution — LGU Relationship & Regulatory Analytics (PA-76.3).)
- operational: segregation-of-duties review — the auditor is independent of the Legal Compliance Officer who remediates; operational: Head of Internal Audit sign-off on the audit report
Pain Points / Risks: - **Sample-blindness risk**: auditing 20–30 of ~205 locations leaves ~175 unaudited; mitigated by the risk-based sample weighting (high-cost LGUs and prior-finding stores) and the W2677 continuous dashboard that covers all locations between audits

- **Finding-recurrence risk**: the same finding repeats year after year (a chronic expired-permit store); mitigated by the SOP-update step and escalation to VP Legal for any finding recurring 2+ cycles
System Touchpoints: - Audit module (links to VS-21 / W120 audit planning, W121 operational audit) — the audit findings register and CAP tracking
- Compliance dashboard (the W2677 dashboard) — the single-pane status the audit samples against
- Regulatory license/permit repository (VS-166) — the permit records audited for currency and display
Time Estimate: ~3 weeks audit fieldwork + ~1 week reporting + remediation tracking absorbed = **~150–200 hours/year** Internal Auditor + Legal Compliance Officer remediation.

steps.activity: Internal Auditor conducts the annual LGU compliance audit at a risk-based sample of locations (20–30/year, weighted to high-cost/high-complexity LGUs and stores with prior findings): verifies permits are current and displayed (W2670–W2675), tax payments complete (W2678/W2679), DOLE postings present (W2681), fire-safety compliance (W2672)

Auditor identifies gaps: expired permits, unpaid taxes, missing postings, non-compliant signage, fire deficiencies; quantifies the penalty exposure for each; rates findings by severity (critical / major / minor)

Legal Compliance Officer implements corrections on a severity-based timeline: critical within 7 days, major within 30 days, minor within 90 days; updates the underlying SOPs to prevent recurrence; tracks the improvement trend into the next cycle

Automation Opportunity: - Incentive-term library per LGU (the standard package each LGU offers) reused across site evaluations; clawback-scenario model auto-generated from the agreement terms
Controls: - CTL-459 (ensure controlled execution — LGU Relationship & Regulatory Analytics (PA-76.3).)
- operational: capex/site-investment approval — links to the VS-20 site-decision gate; operational: CEO + CFO sign-off on any incentive agreement with a >3-year commitment
Pain Points / Risks: - **Clawback risk**: the LGU offers a 5-year tax holiday conditioned on BuildRight operating for 10 years; an early exit (store closure per VS-59) triggers a clawback plus penalty; mitigated by the Legal review surfacing the clawback term and Finance modeling the exit scenario

- **Hidden-condition risk**: the incentive requires a local-employment quota or local-sourcing percentage that constrains operations (BuildRight can't meet the local-sourcing % for specialized import categories); mitigated by the Legal conditions review before signature
System Touchpoints: - Real-estate/site-selection (links to VS-20 / W116 site selection & feasibility, VS-97 corporate real estate) — the site-decision matrix the incentive evaluation feeds
- Contract repository (links to VS-100 / W230) — the incentive agreement with its conditions and clawback terms
- Store-P&L model (links to VS-17 / W26 budget, VS-101 merchandise financial planning) — the incentive-adjusted P&L
Time Estimate: ~30–40 hours per site-selection incentive evaluation × ~12 openings/year = **~360–480 hours/year** COO + Legal + Finance, front-loaded into the site-selection phase.

steps.activity: COO evaluates the LGU incentive package offered under the LGU's Local Investment Code (authorized by RA 7160 §192): tax holidays (often 3–5 years on local business tax), reduced rates, fast-track permitting, infrastructure support, employment incentives (local-hire quotas); compares across the candidate locations

Legal reviews the incentive agreement: enforceability, hidden conditions (employment quotas, local-sourcing requirements, clawback if BuildRight exits early), duration and renewal terms; negotiates additional concessions where BuildRight's investment is material to the LGU

Finance models the incentive impact on the store P&L: tax savings NPV over the holiday period, compliance-cost comparison vs. a non-incentivized LGU (from W2687), clawback risk; COO incorporates the net financial impact into the site-decision matrix

fields.Participants: Legal Compliance Officer, Store Manager, VP Legal

Automation Opportunity: - Response-deadline tracker with auto-escalation; similar-issue matching from the case register to surface prior resolutions
Controls: - CTL-459 (ensure controlled execution — LGU Relationship & Regulatory Analytics (PA-76.3).)
- operational: permit/issue currency tracked in the master; operational: VP Legal review of any settlement >PHP 100K or any trade-suspension outcome
Pain Points / Risks: - **Slow-escalation risk**: a store treats a Notice of Violation as routine and doesn't escalate, missing the response window (often 15–30 days) and converting a curable finding into a final penalty; mitigated by the mandatory 24-hour reporting in step 1 and the case-management auto-escalation on the response deadline

- **Inconsistent-resolution risk**: similar issues get different resolutions across stores because no precedent is captured; mitigated by the case register surfacing prior similar issues and the Officer's resolution playbook
System Touchpoints: - Case management (links to VS-22 / W22.2 government-audit-and-inspection-response, VS-100 / W125 litigation) — the issue register and resolution trail
- Communication/escalation (links to VS-07 / W571, VS-159 corporate security incident pattern applied regulatory-side) — the severity-tiered escalation
- Document repository (links to VS-88) — evidence and correspondence retained per the 10-year rule
Time Estimate: ~1 hour/intake × ~40 issues/month + ~3 hours/resolution × ~25 resolved/month + ad-hoc VP Legal escalations = **~115–150 hours/month ≈ ~1,400–1,800 hours/year (per the itemization)** Legal Compliance Officer + Legal (distributed across the issue volume).

steps.activity: Store Manager reports the issue within 24 hours: an inspection finding, a Notice of Violation, a tax dispute, a DTI consumer complaint (links to W2682), a DOLE labor complaint (links to W2681); provides the initial documentation; Officer logs it in the case-management system
Officer assesses severity: critical (trade-closure risk) → immediate VP Legal escalation; major (penalty exposure >PHP 100K) → Legal team within 48 hours; minor → Officer handles within 7 days

Officer coordinates the resolution: gathers evidence, prepares the response, represents BuildRight in any proceeding, negotiates a settlement where appropriate; documents the outcome; updates the underlying procedure to prevent recurrence

fields.Participants: Legal Compliance Officer, VP Legal, Industry Peers

Automation Opportunity: - Intelligence-feed with source classification and keyword tagging; auto-distribution to the regions facing the flagged issue
Controls: - CTL-459 (ensure controlled execution — LGU Relationship & Regulatory Analytics (PA-76.3).)
- CTL-459 (competition-law conduct in peer forums — links to W2683); operational: VP Legal review of any peer-shared practice before BuildRight adoption
Pain Points / Risks: - **Information-compartmentalization risk**: intelligence gathered in one region isn't shared, so other regions rediscover or get caught by the same issue; mitigated by the quarterly cross-region sharing in step 2 and the central intelligence feed

- **Peer-group-information-hygiene risk**: peer benchmarking shades into anti-competitive information exchange (links to W2683 competition-law compliance); mitigated by the competition-law training framework and legal review of what's shared in peer forums
System Touchpoints: - Regulatory-intelligence feed (links to VS-166 license-portfolio, VS-22 / W22.3 regulatory-change-management) — the canonical store for shared intelligence
- Knowledge management (links to VS-30 / W381 IT knowledge management, VS-88 document control) — the playbooks and practice library
- VS-104 (government affairs & public policy) — the sector-advocacy counterpart (W2691 consumes intelligence; VS-104 may act on it)
Time Estimate: ~4 hours/week network maintenance + ~6 hours/quarter sharing + VP Legal strategy absorbed = **~250–350 hours/year** Legal Compliance Officer.

steps.activity: Officer maintains the intelligence network: Philippine Retailers Association committee participation, a retail peer group (non-competitor informal benchmarking), legal-firm bulletins, and the field intelligence from Regional Managers' LGU interactions (links to W2680 monitoring)

Officer shares intelligence across BuildRight's regions quarterly: a successful practice in one LGU (e.g., a fast-track-permit arrangement) shared for adoption elsewhere; new requirements flagged proactively before they reach BuildRight's LGUs

VP Legal incorporates the intelligence into strategy: identifies sector trends (environmental requirements, single-use-plastic bans, LGU digitalization), anticipates upcoming requirements, and proactively prepares the stores ahead of enactment

fields.Participants: Legal Compliance Officer, VP Legal, Store Manager, LGU

Automation Opportunity: - Closure-decommissioning checklist (permit set → cancel → clearance → archive) sequenced with sign-offs, integrated into the VS-59 closure workflow
Controls: - CTL-459 (ensure controlled execution — LGU Relationship & Regulatory Analytics (PA-76.3).)
- operational: permit-status update to "closed — decommissioned" in the master; operational: VP Legal sign-off on the tax-clearance certifying clean exit
Pain Points / Risks: - **Lingering-liability risk**: a permit isn't formally cancelled and the LGU continues to assess fees/tax on a non-operating location; mitigated by the formal permit-cancellation and tax-clearance in steps 1–2, not just ceasing operations

- **Incentive-clawback risk**: if the closed location had an LGU incentive (W2689) with a minimum-operating-period condition, early closure triggers a clawback; mitigated by the Legal review of the original incentive agreement's clawback term at closure-decision time
System Touchpoints: - Store-closure workflow (links to VS-59 / W45 store closure, VS-37 store lifecycle) — decommissioning is a workstream in the closure plan
- Tax/AP (links to VS-79 / W437 branch de-registration tax clearance, VS-15) — final tax settlement and clearance
- Records retention (links to VS-88 / W256, the 10-year retention rule) — archived permit/tax/correspondence set
Time Estimate: ~40–60 hours per closure decommissioning × ~1.5 closures/year = **~60–90 hours/year** Legal Compliance Officer + Tax Accountant, concentrated in the closure window.

steps.activity: Officer manages the regulatory decommissioning once the VS-59 closure decision is made: LGU notification of closure, permit cancellation (mayor's, FSIC, sanitary, sign), tax-clearance application, final LGU inspection, barangay notification, utilities disconnection, signage removal (links to W2674)

Tax Accountant settles the final obligations: final local business tax (prorated to the closure date per RA 7160), final real property tax, permit-fee reconciliations, obtains the LGU tax clearance certifying no outstanding liability

Officer archives all LGU documentation for the closed location for 10 years per BIR/LGU record-retention requirements (links to VS-88 / W256 document retention, the 10-year TRAIN-law rule); ensures a clean exit without lingering LGU exposure

fields.Participants: VP Legal, Legal Compliance Officer, CFO, CEO

Automation Opportunity: - Annual-report auto-rolled-up from the W2677 dashboard with year-over-year delta and trend; only the strategic analysis added manually
Controls: - CTL-304 (board governance & MCG compliance audit — links to VS-21); operational: Board Audit Committee receipt of the report minuted (governance trail)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Data-stitching risk**: the annual report draws from 7+ workflows (W2677, W2681–W2685, W2687, W2688) and stitching them is error-prone if done by hand; mitigated by the W2677 dashboard as the canonical year-round source, so the report is a rollup not a re-collection

- **Strategic-vs-compliance-imbalance risk**: the report is a compliance scorecard without strategic insight, so the Board can't act on it; mitigated by the explicit strategic-analysis step (step 2) that translates compliance data into investment/priority recommendations
System Touchpoints: - Compliance dashboard (the W2677 dashboard) — the year-round data source the annual report rolls up
- Analytics/BI (links to VS-27 / W113) — the trend visualization and risk heat map
- Board/governance reporting (links to VS-21 / W120 audit planning, VS-36 / W124 corporate secretary) — the Board Audit Committee presentation artifact
Time Estimate: ~2 weeks Officer compilation + ~1 week VP Legal analysis + ~half-day Board presentation = **~140–180 hours/year**, concentrated in the annual reporting cycle.

steps.activity: Legal Compliance Officer compiles the annual dataset: compliance rate by region and LGU, total regulatory cost (from W2687), inspections and findings (from W2688), consumer complaints (from W2682), DOLE results (from W2681), BIR CAS status (from W2685), permit summary (from the W2677 dashboard)
VP Legal adds the strategic analysis: risk assessment by region, emerging regulatory trends (from W2691), relationship quality (from W2686), recommended investments, staffing needs

VP Legal presents to the CEO and the Board Audit Committee (links to VS-21 / W120 audit, VS-36 governance): overall compliance posture, key risks, remediation plans, budget requests; the report becomes the annual governance documentation retained per VS-88
